    Employing the Theory of Taʿlīl in Renewing Zakat Jurisprudence in Indonesia: An Analytical Study of Contemporary Zakat Fatwas Issued by the Indonesian Ulema Council

    ##plugins.themes.bootstrap3.article.main##

    ##plugins.themes.bootstrap3.article.sidebar##

    PDF HTML
    Published Aug 16, 2026
    DOI https://doi.org/10.29117/jcsis.2026.0453
    Copyright Information

    This work is licensed under a .

    Refki Saputra
    Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University Jakarta–Indonesia
    https://orcid.org/0009-0003-0900-0234
    Asep Saepudin Jahar
    Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University Jakarta–Indonesia
    https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4957-5273
    Hamka Hasan
    Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University Jakarta–Indonesia
    https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3000-3777

    Abstract

    Objectives: This research examines the application of the theory of taʿlīl in contemporary zakat fatwas issued by the Indonesian Ulema Council and assesses its contribution to the renewal of zakat jurisprudence in Indonesia.


    Methodology: The research employs inductive and analytical methods. The inductive approach identifies and compiles zakat fatwas issued by the Indonesian Ulema Council, while the analytical approach examines their content, legal reasoning, and contribution to the renewal of zakat rulings.


    Findings: The findings reveal that the Indonesian Ulema Council systematically employs the theory of taʿlīl in renewing zakat jurisprudence. This approach has expanded the scope of zakatable assets and enabled more adaptive mechanisms for zakat collection and distribution in response to contemporary economic realities.


    Originality: This study highlights taʿlīl as a central instrument in contemporary institutional ijtihād and proposes an analytical framework integrating uṣūl al-fiqh and maqāṣid al-sharīʿah in the renewal of zakat jurisprudence.

    The Journal of College of Sharia and Islamic Studies (JCSIS) at Qatar University  is  a peer-reviewed, bilingual, open access journal. It provides a forum for quality research in multidisciplinary classical and contemporary Islamic studies in both Arabic and English from all over the world. Since 1980, JCSIS has established itself as a valuable resource both for scholars and students of Islamic Studies as well as for libraries. JCSIS encourages contributions from all branches of Islamic Studies with a view to deepening historical research on Islam, in both theory and practice, from historical and social-science perspectives since its emergence until modern times.
